results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system, as recorded in VFB. This information is based on the verbatim descriptions provided by VFB, which state that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch that have different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various records related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with parts in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body itself, with counts of [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") images, [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body, among others.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain include [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [[Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain") of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), as well as alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which are further subdivided into subtypes such as core/surface/posterior, anterior-posterior/middle, and dorsal/main/gamma-s/gamma-t classes, according to VFB. VFB records show [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell. VFB holds various data related to Kenyon cell, including [32328](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") images, scRNAseq data, transgene expression data, downstream connectivity classes, and upstream connectivity classes.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are projection neurons from the antennal lobe, as well as sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx, according to VFB. VFB holds [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records of neurons with some part in mushroom body, and [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records of neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body, which may be relevant for a narrower follow-up of mushroom body inputs. The connectome data indicates that the calyx receives sensory interneuron afferents. To learn more about the specific neurons and their connections, you can explore the available data on neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body, which includes [601](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") records, or examine the [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body") tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body.

results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?

The pathway is described as: [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn.

VFB holds data on neurons with some part in the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain") ([1661](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") records) and neurons with synaptic terminals in the adult lateral horn ([1658](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") records), which may be relevant for understanding the connections to the lateral horn. Additionally, VFB has data on transgene expression in the adult lateral horn ([1934](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in adult lateral horn") records) and images of neurons with some part in the adult lateral horn ([17792](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in adult lateral horn") records).

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior and has a unique anatomy and connectivity. It has a large cell body located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, and its large descending axon is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, the giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron enters the ventral nerve cord near the dorsal midline and extends posteroventrally to the mesothoracic neuromere, where it turns ventrolaterally and ends abruptly without branching. In the mesothoracic neuromere, it forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge and at the axonal lateral bend.

VFB holds data on the giant fiber neuron, including [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of DNp01, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting DNp01, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01. The database also contains information on the downstream and upstream connectivity classes for DNp01, with [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records, respectively.

Available driver lines for the giant fiber neuron include P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD}, P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R14A01-p65.AD}, P{R79H02-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD}, and P{VT004455-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R10A12-p65.AD}. Relevant publications on the giant fiber neuron include Phelan et al., 1996, King and Wyman, 1980, Stürner et al., 2025, Dorkenwald et al., 2024, Namiki et al., 2018, Thomas and Wyman, 1984, Koto et al., 1981, Power, 1948, Ito et al., 2014, Kamikouchi et al., 2009, Kennedy and Broadie, 2018, Allen et al., 1998, Bacon and Strausfeld, 1986, Matsuo et al., 2016, and Kim et al., 2020.
